title: How can supply and demand affect a price?
answer: Supply has to do with how much sellers are willing to offer at different prices. Demand has to do with how much buyers are willing and able to buy at different prices. Imagine a market where one stall has five baskets of berries and lots of shoppers want them. The berries might sell at a higher price than they would when many stalls have lots of berries for sale. Other things such as the cost of growing and bringing berries to market can matter too.

title: What does inflation do to what money can buy?
answer: Inflation means prices for many ordinary goods and services are rising overall. If the price of a pack of crayons goes up while most other prices stay the same, that one change alone tells us little about inflation. People who measure it look at prices for a wide group of things. When those prices rise overall, the same amount of money usually buys less than it did before, even if some prices fall.
facts: People who measure inflation compare a group of prices at different times.

title: What is the difference between an import and an export?
answer: When people sell something from one country to someone in another, the sale is an export for the country it comes from. It is an import for the country that buys it. Imagine a store in one country buys pots from a maker abroad. The pots are imports at the store and exports where they were made. Trade can also involve services, such as hiring a person in another country to help design a book.
facts: The same thing can be called an import or an export depending on whose side of the sale you are looking at.

title: Why do people divide up the work of making something?
answer: Imagine making costumes for a class play. One person measures the cloth, one cuts out the shapes, and another stitches them together. If each person practices one job, they can often do it well and do more of it. This way of focusing on part of the work is called specialization. It can help groups make more things together. The group still needs each person’s work, so the steps have to fit one another.
facts: Specialization can happen between people, businesses, or places that focus on different kinds of work.

title: Which services can a town provide together?
answer: People in a town share some services, such as roads, parks, and fire protection. A local government can organize those services for many people at once instead of each household trying to provide its own. Government can use money from taxes to help pay for the workers, equipment, and supplies involved. Different towns arrange services in different ways, and some share a service with nearby places. People can take part in discussions about which services need more support.

title: Why do governments collect taxes?
answer: Taxes are payments that governments require under their laws. Governments use taxes as one way to pay for things they provide, such as some roads and public parks. They can collect different kinds of taxes, including on some purchases, on income, or on property. Which taxes apply depends on where people live or work and what the rules are. Governments use budgets to decide how to spend the money they collect.

facts: Taxes can be collected by different levels of government, such as a country, state, or town.

title: How can a volunteer help a community?
answer: A volunteer chooses to give time to help with a group or project, usually without a paycheck. Volunteers might pick up litter in a park, sort books for a sale, or pack supplies for people who need them. A volunteer often works alongside a group that knows what help is needed. People can choose a project that suits their skills or lets them learn something new. Even a short job can be useful when many people pitch in.

title: How can people keep stories without writing them down?
answer: People can pass on a story by telling it to someone who will tell it again. A repeated line, tune, or pattern can help a listener remember the next part. Families and communities pass along memories, poems, riddles, and other things this way. A teller may change some words to fit a new audience while keeping the main idea. Recordings and notes can help people share what a particular storyteller said.
facts: A story passed from speaker to listener can have more than one version.

title: How does a proverb say a lot in a few words?
answer: A proverb is a short saying that people repeat to share an idea or some advice. For example, “Many hands make light work” tells us that a big job can feel easier when more people help. The saying talks about hands because it gives people a simple picture to remember. People may use a proverb at different times, and what counts as good advice can depend on what is happening.
facts: A proverb usually has a meaning people in a group recognize when they hear it.

title: How do people learn a traditional craft?
answer: Someone learning a traditional craft can watch a person who already knows the work, try a step, and ask what to change. A basket maker might show a learner which plants bend without snapping. A potter can feel when clay is ready to shape and help others learn that feeling. Tools and finished objects can give clues, but practice and time with people who know the craft can keep the skills going.
facts: A skill can stay part of a tradition even when people use it to make new designs.

title: Why do communities hold festivals?
answer: A festival is a time when people take part in shared events. A community might celebrate a season, honor an important date, or share food, music, and stories. Some festivals happen in one building or neighborhood and others spread through a whole town. Children can learn songs or dances by watching people who already know them. The events can change over time when people bring new ideas or move to new places.
facts: A festival can bring together several traditions, such as a parade, a meal, and a way of making music.

title: How can people learn in more than one language?
answer: Some children speak one language at home and learn another in school or when they play with friends. Some classrooms use two or more languages to help students learn. For example, a student might first discuss an idea about plants in a language they know well, then learn the names for the parts of a plant in another language. Both can help the student explain the same idea in different settings.

title: What makes a tradition living heritage?
answer: Living heritage includes things people learn from others and still practice, like telling stories, playing a style of music, or making baskets in a special way. A museum can save a basket, but the skill of making that kind of basket stays alive when people keep doing it and teach it. Traditions can change as new people learn them and find their own ways to use what they learned.
facts: People may call these skills and activities intangible cultural heritage because their meaning cannot be held like an object.

title: What makes a place a World Heritage Site?
answer: Some places hold clues about Earth or human history that people across the world can learn from. Countries can propose special places for an international list kept through UNESCO. A place on that list may be a building, a city, a natural area, or a mix. Protecting it can mean keeping an old structure safe, looking after land and water, or planning how people can visit without damaging the place.

facts: A named World Heritage Site can be important both for its natural features and for its role in people’s lives.
